name: Zhentong (Tony) Ye
intro: I build AI systems that make evidence and model behavior easier to inspect.
availability: Seeking Summer 2027 internships in applied AI and software engineering

methodology.title: How I learn, then build
methodology.intro: I combine 学习观 with the Elephant–Goldfish Model (EGM) as a working methodology: make understanding testable, make intent explicit, and keep implementation accountable to both.

layers.label: LEARNING / 学习观
layers.title: Build a model I can use
layers.text: From 于建国’s 学习观, I take a practical question: can I use what I learned in a situation I have not seen before? I connect an explanation to concrete examples, diagnose where my understanding breaks, and revisit it with new cases.
layers.practice: In my practice: describe the capability, separate recall from understanding, and test transfer with examples outside the learning material.

layers.label: ENGINEERING / EGM
layers.title: Make the design survive a fresh reader
layers.text: I adopt the Elephant–Goldfish Model described by Dave Rensin and presented by Brian Suchy at Northwestern. A context-rich design conversation captures intent and trade-offs; a fresh review without the prior conversation tests whether the written design stands on its own.
layers.practice: In my practice: resolve missing assumptions in the specification, implement within its boundaries, then check the result against explicit acceptance criteria.

steps.title: Understand the task
steps.text: Name the capability, constraints and evidence needed. Check what I can already explain and apply.

steps.title: Write the design
steps.text: Record decisions, interfaces, failure cases and acceptance criteria in a document a new reader can use.

steps.title: Challenge assumptions
steps.text: Ask a fresh reviewer to find ambiguity and counterexamples. Revise the design before implementation.

steps.title: Build and verify
steps.text: Implement a bounded change. Test behavior, retain failures and use new cases to revisit my understanding.

methodology.boundary: This is my synthesis for learning and engineering, grounded in these authors’ work. A passing software test and my ability to explain or apply a concept are separate things to verify.

projects.title: NVIDIA Financial RAG
projects.summary: Ask your PDF a question. Inspect the retrieved evidence, intermediate calculations and an answer draft in a browser lab.
projects.description: Ask a local document a question, then inspect how its pages become chunks, vectors, retrieved evidence and a model-generated draft. A separately packaged Python API explores integration with other applications.
details: Developing an offline Python document index with dense retrieval and source-linked evidence over NVIDIA reports.
Building a reader-device browser workflow with visible parsing, tokenization, vector search, context assembly and native generation stages. The lab lets you choose your own local PDF.
Investigating query formulation, citations, abstention and evaluation against original report evidence. A successful model run produces a draft; financial answer quality still needs evaluation.
Writing the engineering decisions and debugging history as a continuing series, with editable architecture figures and reproducible acceptance records.

projects.title: Fine-Tuning LLaVA-GI
projects.role: Collaborative research · WKU Student Partnering with Faculty
projects.summary: Collaboratively fine-tuned LLaVA-13B for medical visual question answering, from training data preparation to generated-answer evaluation.
projects.description: Collaboratively fine-tuned LLaVA-13B with LoRA/PEFT on Kvasir-VQA, connecting image–question–answer preparation to inference and evaluation.
details: Prepared image–question–answer data, configured training and developed inference scripts with PyTorch and Hugging Face on Linux.
Contributed to generated-answer evaluation with ROUGE-1 and CIDEr and analyzed comparisons with the baseline. The project report records the team's results; they are specific to that experiment.
The SpF final report records ROUGE-1 recall 0.7512 and CIDEr 2.5701 on Kvasir-VQA. These are reported team experiment results, rather than a new reproduction or clinical validation.
Worked with faculty and teammates; a teammate published the code and checkpoint. This is a research prototype, with no clinical deployment claim.

links.label: See how images and questions become an answer

projects.title: OSEF: One-Step Evidence Fusion
projects.summary: Research on retrieving video evidence and planning action sequences from a start–goal query, with controlled benchmark comparisons.
projects.description: Study how a planner can retrieve the right video evidence and predict an action sequence from an answer-redacted start–goal query.
details: Investigated a query-conditioned evidence lattice that keeps all candidate cells available to the planner; a separate branch reports the selected video and time window.
Compared nine planner families with frozen retrieval, hard negatives and leakage checks, measuring evidence selection and procedure planning separately.
The preprint reports a 2.9–10.7 percentage-point FULL-SR gain on four matched same-task COIN/CrossTask settings. FULL-SR requires the correct video and complete action plan together.

In its hard same-task COIN-T3 intervention, masking 48 high-attention cells lowered PLAN-SR from 65.74% to 24.89%; masking 48 random cells left 65.60%, with retrieval unchanged. These are reported study results; read the paper for the setting and limitations.

projects.title: Artisk AI-Agent Product Project
projects.role: Unpaid, collaborative, AI-assisted project · Artisk Inc.
projects.summary: A four-view React agent interface with shared context, explicit tool handoffs and source-grounding checks.
projects.description: Contributed to a React/TypeScript tool-using agent interface with four expert views, shared context and explicit prompt/tool handoffs.
details: Implemented the four-view product interface and shared context so expert workflows could pass information through explicit handoffs.
Modeled a knowledge graph spanning 68 concepts, with 180 nodes, 571 edges and 21 relation types; linked sources through graph expansion and alias matching.
Blocked citations to nonexistent source text and checked the grounding contract with 41 tests. These are project contract checks, rather than a general model-accuracy measure.

projects.title: E-Commerce LLM Agent Platform
projects.role: Agent Engineer / AI Technical Lead · university–industry project
projects.phase: Requirements, data audit and system design
projects.summary: Designing a shared agent platform for customer support, inventory and content workflows for an anonymous e-commerce client.
projects.description: Translating an anonymous cross-border e-commerce client's customer support, inventory and content needs into a proposed shared agent platform.
details: Designing retrieval, policy checks, order/logistics tools, human handoff and auditable customer-support responses, alongside scenarios for citation, privacy and unsafe-action checks.
Identified nine SKUs repeated across sales channels and a replenishment-rule ambiguity that needs resolution before forecasting.
Designing SKU × channel × fulfillment-node P50/P80/P90 forecasts and rolling backtests that account for stockouts and promotions.
Defining product- and brand-grounded image, video-script and social-content workflows with human approval and traceable versions. These workflows remain in design.

projects.title: Overseas Lead Qualification
projects.summary: Comparing trade-data sources and prototyping a source-backed lead qualification workflow for an anonymous B2B manufacturer.
projects.description: Exploring source-backed prospect screening and an AI-assisted qualification workflow for an anonymous B2B manufacturing client.
details: Compared five trade-data providers and prepared source-linked samples and a weighted proof-of-concept scorecard, separating product relevance, buyer identity and contact verification.
Contributed dashboard work, CSV templates and CRM field mapping for a founder-delivered demo.
Designing lead scoring, multilingual product content, RFQ intake and human-reviewed outreach. Provider comparison and prototype work do not establish a deployed sales service.
